leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used to expose a structured macro-analysis workflow that maps scenario factors to multiple asset classes, rather than merely reproducing clicks.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes live macro conditions, portfolio analysis, and tailwinds/headwinds.
Observation reports a factor matrix with readings, effects, net scores, and verdicts for four asset classes.
execution_rationale: The live observation directly verified the central Asset Analysis workflow and a coherent resulting matrix.
execution_evidence: Asset Analysis tab opened successfully.
Factor matrix appeared for US Stocks, US Cash, Gold, and Crypto.
impact_rationale: Consistent macro-to-portfolio interpretation could be useful for investors, though the domain is advisory and the product does not demonstrate consequential execution.
impact_evidence: Portfolio and asset-analysis workflow are explicitly presented.
Observation notes a not-financial-advice warning.
creativity_rationale: The scenario compass and cross-asset factor matrix are a thoughtful application of agent-readable analysis.
creativity_evidence: Scenario controls and macro sliders are part of the live dashboard.
The app connects one macro state to four asset classes.
s2_notes: Strongly verified dashboard workflow; agent-specific tool calls were not directly exercised.
advance_reason: Live central workflow completed and matched the claim.

leverage_rationale: The core idea uses WebMCP's page-owned tool registry as a revocable privacy boundary, with narrow claims instead of raw personal-value tools.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly says permitted claims become tools and raw personal values are never exposed.
Submission describes expiry and getTools visibility as part of consent.
execution_rationale: The privacy wallet is identifiable, but the only attempted permit action produced no visible capability or disclosure change.
execution_evidence: Privacy-focused wallet page loaded with permit controls and disclosure log.
First Permit click showed no visible feedback.
impact_rationale: Preventing raw personal data leakage while enabling useful eligibility checks addresses a serious, broadly applicable agent-safety problem.
impact_evidence: Submission frames over-parameterized eligibility forms and cross-site personal-context leakage as the target problem.
Design uses threshold claims and revocable consent.
creativity_rationale: Treating tool existence itself as consent, combined with no raw-value tool, is an unusually strong conceptual use of WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Tool registry changes are described as the privacy control.
No get_income or date-of-birth tool exists by design.
s2_notes: Excellent concept and clear surface, but the live permission transition was not visibly demonstrated.
advance_reason: High-leverage privacy architecture merits advancement despite weak live interaction evidence.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to a cooperative game in which the agent can hold hidden state or act as a collaborator, beyond ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch defines a human-and-AI ship-repair game.
Submission says tools expose in-game state without extra configuration and enable roleplay.
execution_rationale: The live game shell opened coherently after Begin Repairs, but the AI-dependent repair itself was not completed.
execution_evidence: Begin Repairs transitioned from intro to the ship interface.

impact_rationale: Collaborative games are a meaningful demonstration category, though direct social or economic impact is limited.
impact_evidence: Submission identifies interactive games as a distinctive WebMCP use case.
Live interface presents a playable repair scenario.
creativity_rationale: Using an agent as a cooperative character with information asymmetry is inventive and well matched to WebMCP.
creativity_evidence: Hidden information and AI roleplay are explicit design goals.
Locked repair destinations imply staged collaboration.
s2_notes: Game entry and state transition verified; full cooperative puzzle completion remains unverified.
advance_reason: Distinctive WebMCP-native game concept with a working entry flow.

leverage_rationale: The submission positions WebMCP as a semantic design surface for layouts, diagrams, math, tables, and presentations rather than only button control.
leverage_evidence: Pitch lists structured design operations including images, text, and tables.

execution_rationale: A usable canvas editor loaded, but selecting Text did not visibly create an object or expose the agent-driven workflow.
execution_evidence: Canvas editor with PDF upload, drawing tools, pages, zoom, and import/export was visible.
Text-tool click produced no obvious text object or edit field.

impact_evidence: Submission claims posters, ads, book covers, pages, diagrams, and interactive presentations.
Live editor exposes broad design primitives.

creativity_evidence: Tool vocabulary includes layout templates, canvas inspection, tables, and math.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is used to implement partial, revocable authority for consequential payment operations, separating investigation from money movement.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes investigation tools without release authority and human-granted mandates.
Submission describes bounded amount, rail, beneficiary, and time constraints.
execution_rationale: The live payment desk and Authority view worked and visibly represented identities and the absence of registered capabilities, though mandate negotiation was not exercised.
execution_evidence: Payment queue and authority/audit interface loaded.
Authority tab listed connected identities while capability area reported none registered.
impact_rationale: Bounded agent authority in banking directly addresses high-consequence automation risk and has clear applicability to other operational systems.
impact_evidence: Submission targets partial authority for banks, hospitals, and factories.
Human approval and revocation are central to the described flow.
creativity_rationale: Negotiating a temporary mandate that compiles into an allowed tool is a compelling and original WebMCP pattern.
creativity_evidence: Mandate request is editable before agreement.
Authority boundary is represented in the live UI.
s2_notes: Live authority boundary verified; actual propose/grant/release sequence not tested.
advance_reason: High-stakes, well-aligned WebMCP use case with verified product surface.

leverage_rationale: The stated design compiles a person's temporary field-level choices into an expiring WebMCP tool and rechecks them server-side, making WebMCP central to authorization semantics.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly describes temporary mandates compiled from updatable fields.
Submission explains expiry, live registration, and per-call checks.
execution_rationale: The provided demo timed out twice, so no central workflow or usable product state was observed.
execution_evidence: Navigation timed out during the live observation.
No reliable page state or action result was available.
impact_rationale: Just-in-time, least-privilege, expiring authorization is highly relevant to safe agent actions across business systems.
impact_evidence: Submission contrasts temporary human delegation with long-lived credentials.
Claimed model limits records, fields, and duration.
creativity_rationale: Turning an updatable human permission form into a live expiring tool is a particularly strong WebMCP-specific idea.
creativity_evidence: Tool existence is claimed to reflect current consent.
The design combines field scope, expiry, and server revalidation.
s2_notes: Very strong concept and video evidence exists, but live deployment was unavailable; execution is scored from observed failure.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage, impact, and creativity despite failed live verification.

leverage_rationale: WebMCP is positioned as the live bridge between an agent's user knowledge and the document margin, enabling contextual reading without writing to source text.
leverage_evidence: Pitch describes agent-driven annotations, adaptive density, glosses, and connections.

execution_rationale: The supplied URL did not expose a Marginalia reader or any meaningful workflow.

impact_evidence: Submission targets current chat-box limitations and source-preserving marginalia.

leverage_rationale: The product makes capability itself the learning gate: coaching tools are revoked and exam tools materialize based on demonstrated mastery, a deep use of page-owned WebMCP state.

impact_evidence: Submission centers retrieval practice, diagnosis, and unaided exam behavior.
